abi: abeō, -īre, -iī, -itum — to go away, depart (sg. imper.; pulsus abī, 'go, beaten')
acerbat: acerbō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to make bitter, sharpen, aggravate (3rd sg. pres.)
ades: adsum (assum), -esse, -fuī — to be present, be at hand (2nd sg. pres.; 'you are on the spot')
adicias: adiciō, -ere, -iēcī, -iectum — to add, throw to (2nd sg. pres. subj., jussive; first syllable long, as if adiiciās)
aetolus: Aetōlus, -a, -um — Aetolian; here as a name, Diomedes, from Aetolia (m. nom. sg.)
agger: agger, aggeris (m.) — mound, rampart, earthwork (nom. sg.)
amittes: āmittō, -ere, āmīsī, āmissum — to lose, let go (2nd sg. fut.)
argue: arguō, -ere, -uī, -ūtum — to accuse, charge, prove (+ gen. of the charge) (sg. imper.)
arguet: arguō, -ere, -uī, -ūtum — to accuse, charge, convict (3rd sg. fut.)
arpi: Arpī, -ōrum (m. pl.) — Arpi, city of Apulia founded by Diomedes (nom. pl.)
aufidus: Aufidus, -ī (m.) — the Aufidus, river of Apulia flowing into the Adriatic (nom. sg.)
auspicium: auspicium, -iī (n.) — omen from birds, auspices; command under auspices (acc. sg.)
bone: bonus, -a, -um — good, kind, worthy (m. voc. sg.; 'good king')
bonis: bonum, -ī (n.) — a good thing, benefit, interest; pl. goods (n. abl./dat. pl., here 'the common interests')
cessa: cessō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to hold back, delay, stop (sg. imper.; ne cessa, 'do not stop')
communibus: commūnis, -e — common, shared, general (m./n. abl./dat. pl.; also f.)
concipis: concipiō, -ere, -cēpī, -ceptum — to take in, conceive, harbour (2nd sg. pres.)
consedisse: cōnsīdō, -ere, -sēdī, -sessum — to sit down, settle, sink down (perf. inf.)
crescere: crēscō, -ere, crēvī, crētum — to grow, swell, rise (pres. inf.)
dardanidis: Dardanidēs, -ae (m.) — descendant of Dardanus, a Trojan (dat. pl., Greek patronymic, = Dardanidae)
deficimus: dēficiō, -ere, -fēcī, -fectum — to fail, lose heart, give out (1st pl. pres.)
des: dō, dare, dedī, datum — to give, grant (2nd sg. pres. subj., after quīn: 'from giving')
desolavimus: dēsōlō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to leave desolate, lay waste, empty (1st pl. perf.)
devovi: dēvoveō, -ēre, -vōvī, -vōtum — to vow, devote, consecrate (to the gods below) (1st sg. perf.)
dicique: dīcō, -ere, dīxī, dictum — to say, tell (pres. inf. pass., dīcī, 'to be told, proclaimed') + -que, and
dignisque: dignus, -a, -um — worthy, fitting, suitable (+ abl.) (m./f./n. abl. pl., with hymenaeīs) + -que, and
distinet: distineō, -ēre, -tinuī, -tentum — to hold apart, keep off, hold back (3rd sg. pres.)
drance: Drancēs, -is (m.) — Drances, Latin elder, Turnus's rival in the council (voc. sg., Greek name)
egregiusque: ēgregius, -a, -um — outstanding, excellent, distinguished (m. nom. sg.; + gen. animī) + -que, and
exosa: exōsus, -a, -um — hating, detesting (perf. part. of exōdī, active sense; f. nom. sg., with Victōria)
experiare: experior, -īrī, expertus sum — to try, test, put to the proof (2nd sg. pres. subj., = experiāris; deponent)
extollere: extollō, -ere — to lift up, raise; exalt, magnify (pres. inf.)
exutos: exuō, -ere, -uī, -ūtum — to strip off, strip, deprive (+ abl.) (perf. pass. part., m. acc. pl.; 'stripped of')
factaque: faciō, -ere, fēcī, factum — to make, do; factus (perf. pass. part., n. acc. pl., 'made, forged') + -que, and
fatentur: fateor, -ērī, fassus sum — to admit, confess, declare (3rd pl. pres., deponent)
felixque: fēlīx, -īcis — fortunate, lucky, blessed (m. nom. sg., with Tolumnius) + -que, and
fingis: fingō, -ere, fīnxī, fictum — to shape, form; imagine, pretend (2nd sg. pres.)
fingit: fingō, -ere, fīnxī, fictum — to shape; feign, make oneself out (3rd sg. pres.)
flatusque: flātus, -ūs (m.) — blowing, blast, gust; puffing pride (acc. pl.) + -que, and
foedissime: foedus, -a, -um — foul, hideous, disgraceful (superl. foedissimus; m. voc. sg., 'most foul one')
fortunatusque: fortūnātus, -a, -um — fortunate, lucky, blessed (+ gen. of respect) (m. nom. sg.) + -que, and
fugacibus: fugāx, -ācis — fleeing, swift to flee, timid (m./f./n. abl. pl., with pedibus)
futilis: fūtilis, -e — worthless, empty, untrustworthy (m. nom. sg., with auctor; non futilis, 'of real weight')
genero: gener, -erī (m.) — son-in-law, bridegroom (dat./abl. sg.; here dat. 'for a son-in-law')
habitet: habitō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to dwell, live in, stay (3rd sg. pres. subj., jussive)
hadriacas: Hadriācus, -a, -um — of the Adriatic, Hadriatic (f. acc. pl., with undās)
hostilique: hostīlis, -e — of an enemy, hostile (m./n. abl. sg., with aggere) + -que, and
iliaco: Īliacus, -a, -um — of Ilium, Trojan (m./n. abl. sg., with sanguine)
imus: eō, īre, iī (īvī), itum — to go (1st pl. pres.; imus in adversōs, 'we go against them')
inclusus: inclūdō, -ere, -clūsī, -clūsum — to shut in, enclose (perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg.)
infletaque: īnflētus, -a, -um — unwept, without lament (f. nom. sg., with turba) + -que, and
inhumata: inhumātus, -a, -um — unburied, without burial (f. nom. sg., with turba; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
intacta: intactus, -a, -um — untouched, unscathed, unspent (f. nom. sg., with iuventūs; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
inviolabile: inviolābilis, -e — inviolable, not to be harmed or broken (n. nom./acc. sg., with pignus)
iungas: iungō, -ere, iūnxī, iūnctum — to join, bind, unite (2nd sg. pres. subj., after quīn; iungere foedus, to seal a treaty)
ius: iūs, iūris (n.) — right, law, justice; a claim (acc. sg., here 'his own right')
largus: largus, -a, -um — abundant, lavish, generous (+ gen.) (m. nom. sg., largus opum, 'rich in wealth')
larissaeus: Lārissaeus, -a, -um — of Larissa, Thessalian (city of Achilles' country) (m. nom. sg., with Achillēs)
libertatem: lībertās, -ātis (f.) — freedom, liberty; freedom of speech (acc. sg.)
luat: luō, -ere, luī — to pay, atone for, expiate (3rd sg. pres. subj., jussive; morte luat, 'pay with death')
minetur: mīnor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to threaten, menace (3rd sg. pres. subj., deponent; concessive after licet)
mitti: mittō, -ere, mīsī, missum — to send, dispatch (pres. inf. pass., 'to be sent')
momordit: mordeō, -ēre, momordī, morsum — to bite, gnaw (3rd sg. perf.)
mussant: mussō, -āre, -āvī — to mutter, murmur; hesitate to speak (3rd pl. pres.)
mutabilis: mūtābilis, -e — changeable, fickle, shifting (m./f. nom. sg., with labor)
nobilitas: nōbilitās, -ātis (f.) — noble birth, high rank; nobility (nom. sg.)
obliqua: oblīquus, -a, -um — slanting, sidelong, askance (f. abl. sg., with invidiā; also n. nom./acc. pl.)
obsto: obstō, -āre, -stitī, -stātum — to stand in the way, obstruct, oppose (+ dat.) (1st sg. pres.)
obtestemur: obtestor, -ārī, -ātus sum — to call to witness; implore, beseech (1st pl. pres. subj., hortatory; deponent)
occidimus: occidō, -ere, -cidī, -cāsum — to fall, perish, be ruined (1st pl. perf.; 'we are undone')
oremus: ōrō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to pray, beg, plead for (1st pl. pres. subj., hortatory)
parque: pār, paris — equal, like, alike (f. nom. sg., with tempestās; n. acc. sg.) + -que, and
patriaeque: patria, -ae (f.) — fatherland, native country (dat. sg.; also gen. sg., nom. pl.) + -que, and
patribusque: pater, patris (m.) — father; pl. patrēs, elders, senators (dat./abl. pl.) + -que, and
pavidum: pavidus, -a, -um — trembling, fearful, timid (m. acc. sg.)
poscimus: poscō, -ere, poposcī — to demand, call for, ask (1st pl. pres.; + two accusatives)
praestet: praestō, -āre, -stitī, -stitum — to excel, furnish; show oneself as (3rd sg. pres. subj., concessive after licet)
proicis: prōiciō, -ere, -iēcī, -iectum — to throw forward, cast away, expose (2nd sg. pres.)
proinde: proinde (adv.) — accordingly, so then, therefore (often with an imperative; two syllables by synizesis)
recusem: recūsō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to refuse, decline (1st sg. pres. subj., in a result clause after ut)
regressum: regressus, -ūs (m.) — a going back, return, retreat (acc. sg.)
remittat: remittō, -ere, -mīsī, -missum — to send back, give up, relax, abate (3rd sg. pres. subj., jussive)
replenda: repleō, -ēre, -plēvī, -plētum — to fill again, fill up (gerundive, f. nom. sg., with cūria: 'is to be filled')
revertor: revertor, revertī, reversus sum — to turn back, return (1st sg. pres., deponent in the present system)
revisens: revīsō, -ere, -vīsī — to visit again, revisit, look in on (pres. part., f. nom. sg., with Fortūna)
secundus: secundus, -a, -um — following, second; favourable (m. nom. sg.; haud ūllī secundus, 'second to none')
seditione: sēditiō, -ōnis (f.) — civil strife, faction, riot (abl. sg.; potēns sēditiōne, 'strong in faction')
soceroque: socer, -erī (m.) — father-in-law (dat./abl. sg., here dat.) + -que, and
sternamur: sternō, -ere, strāvī, strātum — to lay low, spread out, strew (1st pl. pres. subj. pass.; 'let us be laid low')
stimulisque: stimulus, -ī (m.) — goad, spur, sting (abl. pl.) + -que, and
tendamus: tendō, -ere, tetendī, tentum — to stretch out, extend (1st pl. pres. subj., hortatory)
timoris: timor, -ōris (m.) — fear, dread, cowardice (gen. sg.; gen. of the charge with arguō)
tollat: tollō, -ere, sustulī, sublātum — to lift, raise up; carry off, win (3rd sg. pres. subj., jussive)
tolumnius: Tolumnius, -ī (m.) — Tolumnius, Rutulian augur and ally of Turnus (nom. sg.)
tona: tonō, -āre, -uī — to thunder, speak loudly, roar (sg. imper.)
ullius: ūllus, -a, -um — any (gen. sg., all genders; ūllīus violentia, 'anyone's violence')
viles: vīlis, -e — cheap, worthless, of little account (f. nom. pl., with animae)
vincat: vincō, -ere, vīcī, victum — to conquer, overcome (3rd sg. pres. subj., jussive; nec vincat, 'let not … overcome')
vulcani: Vulcānus, -ī (m.) — Vulcan, god of fire and the forge (gen. sg.)

__broaden__.consulis: cōnsul, -ulis (m.) — consul, chief Roman magistrate (gen. sg.) · also consulō, -ere, -uī, -ultum — to consult, ask counsel on (2nd sg. pres.: rem consulis)
__broaden__.habitus: habitus, -ūs (m.) — dress, garb, bearing (acc. pl.; also nom. sg.) · also habeō perf. pass. part., m. nom. sg. (habitus auctor, 'held to be')
__broaden__.induat: induō, -ere, -uī, -ūtum — to put on; sē induere (+ abl.), to throw oneself upon, impale oneself on (3rd sg. pres. subj., deliberative) · also concessive after licet (3rd sg. pres. subj.)
__broaden__.larga: largus, -a, -um — abundant, lavish, generous (f. abl. sg., with manū) · also f. nom. sg. (larga copia)
__broaden__.latini: Latīnus, -a, -um — Latin, of Latium (m. nom. pl.; gen. sg.) · also m. voc. pl. (Latīnī, addressed) · also Latīnus, -ī (m.), the king, gen. sg. (arma Latīnī)
__broaden__.insignis: insignis, -e — marked, conspicuous, splendid (f. gen. sg.; also m./f. nom. sg.) · also insigniō, -īre — to mark out, adorn (2nd sg. pres.: tropaeīs insignīs agrōs)
__broaden__.ventosa: ventōsus, -a, -um — windy, stormy, wind-swept (n. acc. pl.; ventōsa aequora) · also f. abl. sg. (ventōsā in linguā)
__broaden__.vocet: vocō, -āre, -āvī, -ātum — to call, summon (3rd sg. pres. subj., indirect question) · also concessive subj. after quamvis (quamvis … vōcet) · also after ōrō, ut omitted (vocet ōrō)
__broaden__.solitae: soleō, -ēre, solitus sum — to be accustomed, be wont; perf. part. (semi-deponent), f. nom. pl. · also f. gen. sg. as adj. (solitae virtūtis)
__broaden__.solum: solum, -ī (n.) — ground, soil, land (acc./nom. sg.); also sōlus, alone (n. acc. sg.) · also n. nom. sg. (sōlus, alone: hoc sōlum nōmen) · also adv., only, merely · also m. acc. sg. (mē sōlum)
__broaden__.tantum: tantus, -a, -um — so great; tantum (n. acc. sg.), so great a thing; (adv.) only, so much · also m. acc. sg. (tantum dolorem) · also n. acc. sg. adj. (tantum rōbur)
